title: Digital Read Serial
description: Read a pushbutton with a pull-down resistor and print its state (0 or 1) to the Serial Monitor.

steps.clip: Let's build a circuit that tells us when a button is pressed. Grab a pushbutton, a 10k resistor, and some jumper wires.
Push the pushbutton into the breadboard so it straddles the center gap, with two legs on each side.
hints: The button must sit across the middle gap of the breadboard so two legs land above it and two below.
The two legs on each side are already connected to each other inside the button — pressing it joins the two sides.

steps.clip: Run a wire from digital pin 2 to one of the button's legs.
hints: Connect pin 2 to any leg on one side of the button — both legs on that side are the same connection.
You'll add a resistor to this same row next.

steps.clip: Add a 10k resistor from that same row down to a free row — this will pull pin 2 low when the button isn't pressed.
hints: Plug one resistor leg into the same column as the button leg and the pin 2 wire.
Leave the resistor's other leg in an empty column for now — that one goes to ground.

steps.clip: Connect the resistor's other leg to GND with a wire.
hints: Run a wire from the resistor's free leg to one of the Arduino's GND pins.
This pull-down resistor keeps pin 2 reading LOW whenever the button is open.

steps.clip: Connect the button's other side to 5V.
hints: Wire 5V to the pair of legs on the button you haven't used yet — the other side of the gap.
Pressing the button will now connect 5V through to pin 2, so it reads HIGH.

steps.clip: Upload the sketch and open the Serial Monitor — you'll see 0 when the button is released and 1 when it's pressed.
